summary:
--- PART 1/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / discarded the report / said the trace itself misread the probe — "We need answer only Python source defining def strategy(history, rng), no other top-level defs/annotations/decorators/markdown. Need improve parent."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving tit-for-tat that starts C, defects if opponent last D, and offers C after mutual DD. The trace simulates many population strategies (grim, TFT, always C, forgiving TFT, WSLS) and considers endgame defection, probing, and exploitation. It plans to add last-round defection and possibly adaptive probing while preserving cooperation against retaliators.

--- PART 2/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So against parent: parent starts C. Slot 1 starts C. They cooperate until round 10 (n=10)."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates first, retaliates only after an opponent defect, and forgives after a single opponent defection. The trace simulates the parent against slots 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11, including slot 1's periodic defections against pure cooperators. It proposes an adaptive probing/exploitation strategy that defects periodically against forgiving opponents, backs off when punished, and defects on the last round.

--- PART 3/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So parent's fitness of 278.85 is actually quite good. The losses must come from other strategies."
STRATEGY: Parent is a mostly-TFT strategy with special rules (opD==1, opC>=3, endgame). Simulated against slot1, a strategy that defects every 5 rounds under perfect cooperation and every 9 rounds otherwise. Changed by considering defecting once early to break slot1's perfect-cooperation condition, but concluded parent already does this via retaliation.

--- PART 4/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "But parent's fitness is 278.85. So there must be other strategies in the archive that are not in the population source, or the population source is not the entire set of opponents."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT-like strategy that cooperates first, retaliates on opponent defection, and forgives single defections. The trace simulates parent against population slots, Always D, random, Pavlov, GTFT, and slot8, and considers adding last-round defection and probe-and-exploit rules. It proposes only defecting when the opponent has already defected, to avoid triggering grim strategies.

--- PART 5/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given all this, the safest and most effective improvement is to add endgame defection on the last round."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy that cooperates until opponent defects, retaliates, and has a forgiveness rule for DD spirals. The trace simulates parent against slot1, slot3, slot8, slot9, grim, Always D, Random, TFT, and Pavlov, and considers adding endgame defection, probabilistic forgiveness, and switching to Always D when opponent defection rate is high. It proposes adding last-round defection and possibly a rule to defect when opponent's defection rate exceeds a threshold while our own defection rate is low.

--- PART 6/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Let's design a strategy:" and "Let's write the new strategy based on parent, but with last round D."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT that retaliates on opponent D, breaks DD after two DDs, and forgives isolated defections. Simulated against population strategies (slot1, Always D, Random, slot8, slot2) to test thresholds. Changed by adding last-round D and a one-way switch to always-D if opponent defected >50% while the strategy cooperated >50%.

--- PART 7/7 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "We'll keep the parent's TFT logic, add last round D, and add the scan for high opponent defection while we are cooperating."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving TFT with special-case rules (mutual-defection forgiveness, short-history handling, triple-defect punishment, etc.). Simulated against Always D, Random 50%, retaliatory, and slot1 opponents. Changed by adding a last-round defection and a scan that switches to always-D if the opponent defected more than half the time while the strategy defected less than half the time (checked from round 10 onward).
